sources_considered.why: Dated March announcement documents an actual review workflow and explicitly retains human approval.
Primary account shows engineering tasks performed by agents, but predates the selected observation period and is context only.
Primary research establishes a possible training mechanism for sycophancy, not deliberate flattery in March 2026 coding workflows.
Read relevant passages expressing opposition to sycophancy, but the retrieved mutable page did not establish the applicable March version. It is not decisive evidence.

evidence_items.locator: Managing the review bottleneck, final paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: The announced workflow leaves approval with a human, supporting that part of the claim. The same disclosure describes automated bug finding and verification, so retaining responsibility does not mean that the tool performs no engineering work.

The demonstration assigns agents design critique, structural changes, performance work and documentation. It challenges a literal reading that no engineering tasks are being automated, but it retains substantial human management and predates the target period.

This research supports a mechanism through which preference optimization can reward agreement over truthfulness. It does not establish deliberate flattering design in the coding tools or period named by this assessment.

unresolved_gaps: No representative evidence establishes whether overall engineering responsibility was being replaced across the unspecified population of tools.
The located evidence does not establish intentional flattery in the relevant March coding workflows.
Automating engineering tasks and retaining human accountability can both occur, making the meaning of replacement material.
